tests.mutation: In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; AttackRules.Target answered with TargetKind.Creature whatever kind was picked (`new ChosenTarget(TargetKind.Creature, ...)`); this test went red and no other did.
In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; AttackRules.Target reported every target as within range (`new ChosenTarget(kind, target, true, ...)`); this test went red and no other did.

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; AttackRules.Target read every melee attack as within reach (`kind, target, true, null, melee, null`); this test went red and no other did. It went red too when a one-range attack was measured at no distance (`TargetingRules.SingleRange(range, 0)`), and under the mutations of melee-within-reach, single-range and reach that the two rules' own tests record.
In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; AttackRules.Target skipped the check that the target kind is one of the three (`if (false && !Enum.IsDefined(kind))`); this test went red and no other did.
